To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Russian tagging model trained on the Russian National Corpus (RNC) dataset achieves 98.5% accuracy and the Russian dependency parsing model achieves 91.5% accuracy on RNC dataset.

(i) Russian tagging model based on maximum entropy classifier outperforms Russian tagger in the current version of Stanford CoreNLP (ii) Russian dependency parser based on neural network classifier outperforms the Russian dependency parser in the current version Stanford CoreNLP.

the models of Russian tagging and dependency parsing are successfully implemented in Stanford CoreN LP toolkit, and the results are comparable with the best results of Russian tagging and parsing in the literature, but there is still much space for improvement.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of the Russian language module for the Stanford CoreNLP natural language processing toolkit, which provides a set of tools for processing natural language texts, including tokenization, sentence segmentation, part-of-speech tagging, named entity recognition, parsing, semantic role labeling, and coreference resolution.
implementing the Russian language models in Stanford CoreN LP toolkit and with evaluation of the quality of the models on the Russian text corpus.

the following questions: (i) what linguistic features are needed to build a robust tagger and parser for Russian, (ii) how can these features be used to build a robust model, (iii) how can these models be implemented in Stanford CoreNLR toolkit.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results of the experiments are quite promising, especially in the case of tagging, where we obtained a very good result of 97.5% F-score on the Russian UD treebank.
the models trained on the data used in the paper give a satisfactory result in tagging, and a good result in parsing.
the models trained with the proposed data and features give good results on the standard test sets, but there is still a lot to do for the Russian NLP.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Russian language is well represented in the Stanford NLP toolkit.
we implemented Russian language support in Stanford CoreN LP, trained and evaluated the tagging model and dependency parser model.
we were able to implement Russian models in CoreNLP toolkit that are able to tag and parse Russian texts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the models are able to produce good results for Russian, comparable to those for more widely used languages such as English.
the Russian language models are not worse than the English ones and that they can be easily integrated in Stanford CoreN LP.
it is possible to build a Russian language model for CoreNLP that is competitive with the best available Russian NLP tools.
